title: CRLR/85/2013 of LAXMI DEVI Vs PAWAN SINGH PANWAR

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No. 85 of 2013
Laxmi Devi and Another
 ...Revisionists
Vs.
Pawan Singh Panwar
...Respondents
Mr. Siddhartha Singh, Advocate for the revisionists.
Mr. R.P. Nautiyal, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. Prashant Khanna, Advocate for
the respondent.
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J (Oral)
 Before venturing to observe on merits of the criminal
revision, few facts, which has been brought to the knowledge of the
court by the learned counsel for the parties are to the effect that the
revisionist herein has filed a First Appeal under Section 19 of the
Family Court's Act, being First Appeal No. 63 of 2013 'Laxmi Devi
vs. Pawan Singh Panwar' (the records of which were summoned from
Registry and perused the same), wherein, she has challenged a
judgment and decree dated 25.03.2013 passed by the Court of
Additional Judge, Family Court, Rishikesh, Dehradun, in Original
Suit No. 65 of 2010 'Pawan Singh Panwar vs. Laxmi Devi', whereby,
the proceedings under Section 13 filed by the respondent (husband)
was allowed and the matrimony, which was solemnized between them
was ultimately dissolved by the decree dated 25.03.2013.
2. When this First Appeal was instituted, as back as on
04.04.2013, which remained pending before Division Bench of this
Court. Ultimately in the First Appeal the parties were called upon to
appear in person and after putting in appearance the matter was placed
before the Registrar Judicial so as to make an effort for settlement,
and consequent thereto, a settlement was shown to have been arrived
at between the parties, as would be apparent from the order sheet of
the First Appeal, which was duly endorsed before the respective
counsels for the parties, as well as the parties themselves, thereby

2
lying down as many as six conditions to be adhered to inter se
between the parties, to sustain the decision of decreeing of Suit of
respondent (husband) for dissolution of marriage solemnized on
14.01.2009. As a consequence thereto, the condition imposed was that
the parties have settled to decide the dispute on the remittance of a
permanent alimony under Section 25 of Cr.P.C. to the tune of Rs. 11
lakhs, which was settled by the said mediation report dated
23.04.2019 to be paid by husband-respondent to the revisionist (wife).
3. There was a direction that in compliance thereto the
respondent (husband) was directed to pay a sum of Rs. 6 lakhs by way
of a demand draft directed to be made payable prior to 27.05.2019, in
order to make the settlement of 23.04.2019, to be effective. Later on,
the matter was taken up before the Division Bench of this Court and
the Division Bench vide its judgment dated 28.05.2019 has observed
that in pursuance to the settlement of 23.04.2019 the husband has
remitted a demand draft of Rs. 6 lakhs and which was handed over to
the revisionist (wife) before the Division Bench of this court itself,
and then thereafter, there was a further direction that the balance
amount out of total Rs. 11 lakhs as settled to be paid as against the
permanent alimony, would be remitted by the respondent (husband) in
monthly installments of Rs. 1 lakh each. Meaning thereby, since
28.05.2019 as of now about five installments were supposed to be
paid by the respondent. Since, the period has lapsed and there is
nothing adverse argued by the counsel regarding payment of balance
five monthly installments to the revisionist, the presumption would be
that as of now entire permanent alimony stands paid.
4. The Court expects that in all probability since there had
been no proceeding further carried by either of the parties in
pursuance to the Division Bench's judgment dated 28.05.2019, in all
probability it is expected that the respondent must have complied the
directions of the Division Bench.

3
5. Be that as it may, the present criminal revision has been
preferred by the revisionist (wife) questioning the impugned judgment
dated 25.03.2013 as rendered by the Court of Additional Judge,
Family Court, Rishikesh, District Dehradun in Miscellaneous Case
No. 48 of 2011 'Laxmi Devi and Another vs. Pawan Singh Panwar',
whereby, in the said proceedings under Section 125 of Cr.P.C. an
application preferred by the revisionist has been partly allowed for
awarding maintenance and the Court had awarded the maintenance
only in favour of the revisionist no. 2, i.e. Master Shaurya, and the
amount of maintenance as determined therewith in pursuance to the
impugned judgment under challenge in the present criminal revision,
was determined to be payable at the rate of Rs. 1,000/- per month,
which was directed to be made payable to the revisionist no. 2.
6. On account of the fact that the parties have already
settled their dispute before the Division Bench, as would be apparent
from the Division Bench's judgment referred above, a permanent
alimony has also been settled under Section 25 of the Hindu Marriage
Act, inter se between the parties, this criminal revision, as such as a
matter of fact, in view of the judgment of this Court dated 28.05.2019
has lost its relevance. In all probability, the revision might have lost
its significance with the passage of time. Hence, this criminal revision
is closed subject to the fulfillment of the conditions imposed by the
Division Bench's judgment dated 28.05.2019.
7. Being conscious of the procedural fact as involved in the
present criminal revision, since it is emanating from the proceedings
under Section 125 of Cr.P.C., which itself statutorily entails a right of
recall of order passed in the proceedings under Section 125 Cr.P.C.,
also in case if the conditions of the Division Bench's judgment has not
been complied with, it would amount to that the revision to be still
sustainable and, in that eventuality, either of the parties may file an
appropriate application for recall, if at all required, seeking recall of
today's judgment in the present criminal revision.

4
8. Consequently, in view of the aforesaid observation, the
present criminal revision is closed in the light of the Division Bench's
judgment dated 28.05.2019.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 08.01.2020
Pooja
